To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the market mechanism is endogenously determined by the trade-off between the benefits of price competition and the costs associated with the lack of price competition.
the seller is better off under posted pricing if the quality of the goods sold in the market is sufficiently high.

(1) the seller will always prefer negotiated pricing over posted pricing; (2) the buyers will prefer posted pricing over negotiated pricing if the quality uncertainty is small; and (3) the buyers will always prefer negotiated over posted pricing when the quality uncertainty is large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What determines the choice of a trading rule?
the following question: Under what conditions will a market with imperfectly informed buyers adopt a trading mechanism that allows the seller to exploit his customers?
the impact of imperfect information on the pricing mechanism in a market with a single product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, under the conditions of this paper, the market participants will choose the pricing mechanism that is most efficient for the market as a whole, but that the seller will be the residual claimant.
negotiated pricing is the equilibrium in the case of low quality uncertainty, whereas posted pricing is the equilibrium when quality uncertainty is high.
the market mechanism is a crucial determinant of the quality level that the market will select.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the presence of quality uncertainty, negotiated pricing will prevail in markets where the seller has a large market power, whereas posted pricing will be the dominant pricing mechanism in markets with a small market power.
the market participants choose negotiated pricing if the market is sufficiently small and if quality uncertainty is sufficiently high.
price competition is not a prerequisite for an efficient market outcome, but it can be an important instrument in the seller's hands to exploit the buyer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice between posted and negotiated pricing depends on the degree to which the market is characterized by a lack of price competition.
the market participants' information asymmetry is the driving factor in the choice of trading mechanism.
the equilibrium pricing mechanism in a market is determined by the interplay between bargaining power and the degree of quality uncertainty.
